newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Australian coal purchase fuels Ingwe share.
newsitem.headline: Australian coal purchase fuels Ingwe share.

text.p: More than nine million rand was traded in Ingwe Coal Corp by Tuesday noon, holding the share steady and dealers said interest was due to the South African company completing its acquisition of Coal Mines Australia Ltd.
By 1030 GMT Ingwe was steady at 37 rand after touching 37.20 earlier. It had traded 247,900 shares.
"It's not moving but there are big volumes going through. This is typical of Ingwe. It sits and sits and then gets very active," one dealer said.
"We seldom see trades this size in Ingwe and it looks like it's the same guys as yesterday. Yes, I would definitely say it had something to do with the deal," he added.
Last week Ingwe completed its purchase of CMAL which it plans to make one of Australia's biggest coal producers and exporters. The acquisition cost A$230 million.
CMAL is expected to produce five million tonnes of coal in 1997 and Ingwe said it planned to boost production to 20 million tonnes a year within the next 10 years.
